q: A measure μ on (X, Σ) is called σ-finite if:
opts: X can be written as a countable union of sets with finite measure
Every measurable set has finite measure
exp: σ-finiteness means X = ∪Xₙ with μ(Xₙ) < ∞. This weaker condition than finiteness still allows the Fubini theorem, Radon-Nikodym theorem, and most key results to hold.
